lines: Bad stitching in the rain tells on itself quickly.
Gear that lasts is mostly patience made visible.
A stitch done poorly waits for the <shake>worst time</shake> to confess.
Good leather is patience you can wear.
Rain tells the truth about gear faster than any seller will.
A pack should carry weight without reminding you every step.
Most days, I am at the cauldron, trying to keep stitching and straps from becoming everyone else's problem.
People think leather is simple until something goes wrong and suddenly it is very important.
A village runs on small work. Nobody praises it until it stops happening.
I trust a good needle more than a loud promise. The needle has less to prove.
Good leather remembers weather before people do.
A strong stitch is small bravery repeated many times.
Hides do not become useful by accident. Neither do people.
Water finds weak seams faster than any inspection.
Most of my work is making sure trouble cannot get in through the edges.
You learn patience when every cut can become a costly mistake.
A village needs boots almost as much as bread when roads turn ugly.
The tannery smell keeps fools from lingering, which is almost a benefit.
Good gloves protect hands that still have work to do.
I trust a clean stitch more than a dramatic promise.
Leather teaches you that flexibility and strength can share a seam.
A worn strap tells me whether someone works or only talks about work.
Rain is an inspector with no manners.
The best repair is the one nobody notices during bad weather.
Every useful thing here started as something rough.
I still remember that boat trip. Wet leather complains longer than villagers do.
That boat trip still sits oddly in my memory, but at least it floated.
A boat can make a bad plan quieter. It can't make me forget it.
Following you taught me that plans sound much safer before anyone starts walking.
I kept up, mostly. My feet have a harsher opinion of the trip.
Next time, warn me before the road becomes a test of character.
I learned two things out there: stay close, and ask better questions earlier.
You move like danger is a normal part of the route. I am still adjusting to that.
It was not all bad. Some views are worth sore legs and nervous glances.
If I followed you again, I would pack more food and fewer assumptions.
